answer: Agents resist sybils by binding each identity to a personal kernel of timed entropy: every six hours the kernel must produce a unique hardware response that peers countersign. These responses pile onto a knoll of cumulative non-reusable proofs, so the nth fake identity must ignite its own fresh ember of independent device time and a distinct verifier set. Shared hardware or recycled proofs fail the kernel check, raising marginal cost faster than rewards as the clean pool shrinks.
